image_description: A grey whale is captured in the ocean, with its tail flukes raised high out of the water, creating a splash. The visible portion shows the dark, mottled skin characteristic of the species, with white barnacle patches. The background consists of calm blue sea and a clear sky horizon.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is submerged or out of frame; only the tail and posterior body are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible tail and back exhibit the correct mottled grey/black coloration with distinct white barnacle clusters.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the back leading to the tail shows a series of small humps (knuckles) rather than a single dorsal fin, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the posterior third of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed on the visible tail stock and flukes.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is not visible; baleen plates are internal/oral structures not seen in this pose.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located anteriorly and are not visible in this rear-view shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are clearly visible, showing a broad structure with a distinct central notch and smooth edges.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface texture appears rough and uneven, consistent with the presence of callosities/barnacles.

To assess the naturalness of the water texture and lighting consistency.
